videos.oembed_title: Engineering voice agents: Latency, quality, and scale — Rishabh Bhargava, Together AI
videos.watch_for: Targets for each stage of the cascade (STT, LLM time-to-first-token, TTS first audio, network) and what changes with speech-to-speech. Use them to fill your per-stage latency budget.
videos.why_this_one: Recent, chaptered conference talk that gives concrete per-stage numbers.

videos.oembed_title: How to build the world's fastest voice bot: Kwindla Hultman Kramer
videos.watch_for: Measure voice-to-voice latency as the silence the user hears, and keep it separate from each service's own timings. That is the measurement habit Exercise 1 asks for.
videos.why_this_one: Daily/Pipecat CEO, the team behind the primer, so it carries the same vendor view the lesson warns about.

videos.oembed_title: Pipecat TV - Episode 2 - Smart Turn v3

videos.oembed_title: Why ChatGPT Keeps Interrupting You — Dr. Tom Shapland, LiveKit
videos.watch_for: End-of-turn detection with conversational context, and why a backchannel ('mm-hm') is not an interruption, which is the job of LiveKit's turn modes and false-interruption handling.
videos.why_this_one: LiveKit's own speaker on the official AI Engineer channel; chaptered. A little over 25 min, but every chapter is on topic.

videos.oembed_title: Building voice agents with OpenAI — Dominik Kundel, OpenAI
videos.watch_for: After a barge-in, trim the history to what the listener actually heard, not to what the model generated. Exercise 2 implements exactly that.
videos.why_this_one: OpenAI developer-experience lead; the chapter 'Track what the listener actually heard'.
videos.segment_source: ai.engineer talk page chapters (site-generated from the transcript, not uploader chapters): "Track what the listener actually heard"
videos.code_note: Watch for the idea, not the code: June 2025 Agents SDK realtime code; ai.engineer notes the launch-era code removed the interrupted transcript instead of trimming it. Follow the lesson.
